::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** September 10, 1858.  
**From:** Otterbourne, Winchester,  
**Manuscript:** MS location unknown.  Printed in Coleridge, <i>[Life](other_books/otherbook_40.qmd)</i> 220
:::

My dear [Anne](people/person_1582.qmd)-
[Graham](people/person_321.qmd) and [James Yonge](people/person_1804.qmd)[^1] went away before we were up this morning, and it would all have seemed like a dream if [Duke](people/person_1599.qmd) had not been there at breakfast. [Alice Moberly](people/person_1025.qmd) came out in the fly that fetched us, and spent the whole day with [mamma](people/person_1606.qmd); they gave the schools some buns and sugared negus by way of celebration, and I think mamma did very well.

I think we must have made a very pretty procession; [Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) went into church first with [Mrs. Walter](people/person_130.qmd) and James, and then when [the Colonel](people/person_1461.qmd) brought [Frances](people/person_1604.qmd), we six bridesmaids lined the pretty lych-gate, all hung with festoons of flowers, and closed in behind her.[^2] She had been a good deal overcome while waiting at home, and much more in real need of sal-volatile than [Jane](people/person_1042.qmd) was, and I believe she had a very bad headache all day, but she was quite right as long as she had anything to do, and was very bright and pretty at the luncheon, with little [Herbert](people/person_1463.qmd) upon her lap. Poor [Louisa](people/person_616.qmd) was very much distressed, and little [Gertrude](people/person_1462.qmd) looked so pale, and clung to her every moment she could.[^3] There were about thirty-six people at the luncheon, at a table arranged like a T. . . . Julian looked very nice and well, and one longs for their coming home to eat the great piece of honeycomb which [Kezia](people/person_713.qmd)'s mother has most appropriately presented....

The school-children scattered laurel leaves and flowers, and the church was very full of people. Julian told me to send thanks for the pretty little obelisk and the two plates---how very well the sweetwilliam is done, and I have a special delight in the white flower at the base of the obelisk. [Mr. Keble](people/person_798.qmd) is going to give him a big Bible. I have so many letters to write that I cannot go on any longer-

Your most affectionate
C. M. Yonge

---

[^1]: Graham Colborne and James Yonge had come to Otterbourne to attend the marriage (9 Sept 1858) of Julian Yonge to Emma Frances Walter (1839-1913).  James Edmund Yonge (b. 1843) was the son of Vice-Admiral Edmund Yonge, brother of Lady Seaton and Uncle Yonge.
[^2]: Mrs Walter was Frances’s stepmother. Lieut.-Colonel Edward Walter (1804-1862) of the  3rd Bombay Light Cavalry, had married, first, Mary Emma Coulthard and, secondly (1853) Caroline Janetta Bignell.
[^3]: Louisa (1840-1916) and Gertrude Walter (1849-1897) were Frances’s younger sisters. Herbert was her half-brother.
